name: bowel obstruction overview
title: A distended abdomen: painless with bulging flanks is ascites; painful, central and tympanic is obstruction, sorted on X-ray into small bowel (adhesive after previous surgery, or non-adhesive) and large bowel (closed loop), each with presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order, plus the FATAL signs that send any obstruction to surgery

root.title: Distended abdomen: ASCITES or OBSTRUCTION? Then WHERE, and is it an ADHESION?
lines: OBSTIPATION (no stool AND no gas) is the key feature of obstruction
exam every time: hernias · rectal exam for masses · SURGICAL SCARS · palpable masses

groups.title: PAINFUL, central, tympanic: OBSTRUCTION
lines: abdominal X-ray series: upright + supine abdomen, upright chest (free air?)
dilated if > 3 cm small bowel · > 6 cm colon · > 9 cm cecum (3-6-9)

tiers.title: SMALL bowel: any previous SURGERY (scars)?
lines: RED FLAGS for ischemia or impending perforation (FATAL): Fever, Acidosis (lactate ↑), Tachycardia, Abdominal pain (peritonitis), Leukocytosis · also hypotension

head: h
Adhesive small bowel obstruction
ADHESIONS: the #1 cause
inv: confirms, grades, shows bowel at risk
tx: not past the block in 24-48 h → SURGERY

head: h
Non-adhesive small bowel obstruction
a RED FLAG
tx: will NOT settle with time and an NG tube

head: h
Large bowel obstruction
NEOPLASM #1 · diverticular disease · volvulus
pres: competent ileocecal valve: blocked at both ends, cannot decompress
tx: every complete mechanical large bowel obstruction
